children.translated_text: Under the pretext of meditation, you contemplate — O <s>Kāma</s>! Opening your eyes for a moment,
[you see] these people afflicted by the arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One), yet though a protector, you do not save them.
Your compassion is false; you are more cruel — what other man could be [more so] than you?

children.text: serṣyaṃ māravadhūbhirityabhihito bodhau jinaḥ pātu vaḥ // Nā_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Thus addressed with jealousy by the wives of <s>Māra</s>, may the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), [seated] in awakening, protect you! // Nā 1.1 //
With his bow drawn by <s>Kāma</s>, with <s>Māra's</s> heroes whose swift strikes are defeated,
with the host of celestial women whose glances are stirred by frowns, proud stretching, and smiles,
with the <s>Siddhas</s> whose heads are humbly bowed, and with <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) whose body is bristling with wonder —

children.text: dhyāyan bodheravāptāvacalita iti vaḥ pātu dṛṣṭo munīndraḥ // Nā_1.2 //
children.translated_text: may the Lord of Sages, seen meditating unmoved at the attainment of awakening, protect you! // Nā 1.2 //
The illustrious <s>Harṣa</s> is a skillful poet; this assembly, too, is a connoisseur of merit;

children.text: loke hāri ca bodhisattvacaritaṃ nāṭye ca dakṣā vayam /
children.translated_text: the story of the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> conduct is captivating in the world, and we are skilled in drama.
Even a single one of these [qualifications] would be a ground for attaining the desired fruit — how much more so

children.text: rmadūbhāgyopacayādayaṃ samuditaḥ sarvo guṇānāṃ gaṇaḥ // Nā_1.3 //
children.translated_text: when, by the abundance of my good fortune, this entire collection of merits has come together! // Nā 1.3 //
O devoted one to the welfare of brahmins, servants, and kinsmen! O <s>haṃsī</s> (swan-lady) of the lake of my house, of gentle disposition!
O noble lady who [blooms like] a lotus only at the moon of your own husband — attend to [your] duties first. // Nā 1.4 //
To render service to my parents, having renounced the sovereignty that came in succession,
I shall go to the forest this very day, just as <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>. // Nā 1.5 //

children.text: rāgasyāspadamityavaimi na hi me dhvaṃsīti na pratyayaḥ
children.translated_text: I know it is the abode of passion; nor do I believe that it is destructible;

children.text: kṛtyākṛtyavicāraṇāsu vimukhaṃ ko vā na vetti kṣitau /
children.translated_text: who on earth does not know that it is averse to the examination of what should and should not be done?
Even though blameworthy, this youth, being under the sway of the senses, could be for [one's] delight —

children.text: bhaktyā yāti yadītthameva pitarau śuśrūṣamāṇasya me // Nā_1.6 //
children.translated_text: if it passes with devotion in just this way, as I attend upon my parents. // Nā 1.6 //

body.text: tiṣṭhan bhāti pituḥ puro bhuvi yathā siṃhāsane kiṃ tathā?

children.text: yat saṃvāhayataḥ sukhaṃ tu caraṇau tātasya kiṃ rājake?
children.translated_text: What is the happiness of ruling compared to the joy of massaging my father's feet?

children.text: kiṃ bhukte bhuvanatraye dhṛtirasau bhuktojjhite yā guroḥ?
children.translated_text: What is eating in the three worlds compared to that contentment when my elder has eaten and left [the rest]?

children.text: āyāsaḥ khalu rājyamujjhitagurustatrāsti kaścid guṇaḥ? // Nā_1.7 //
children.translated_text: Kingdom is but toil when one has abandoned one's elders — what virtue is there in that? // Nā 1.7 //

body.translated_text: What is it to stand on a throne on earth compared to standing before one's father?

children.text: nyāyye vartmani yojitāḥ prakṛtayaḥ santaḥ sukhaṃ sthāpitā
children.translated_text: The subjects have been set on the righteous path; the virtuous have been comfortably established;

children.text: nīto bandhujanastathātmasamatāṃ rājye ca rakṣā kṛtā /
children.translated_text: the circle of kinsmen has been brought to a state equal to myself; protection of the kingdom has been provided;
the wish-fulfilling tree, yielding fruits exceeding desires, has been given to the suppliant —

children.text: kiṃ karttavyamataḥ paraṃ kathaya vā yatte sthitaṃ cetasi // Nā_1.8 //
children.translated_text: what more is to be done beyond this? Tell me, or say what is fixed in your mind. // Nā 1.8 //
With its sandalwood trees streaming sap from being rubbed against the temple-walls of intoxicated directional elephants,
with its caverns and ravines resounding, lashed by the waves of the ocean,
with its pearl-cliffs reddened by the lac from the feet of <s>Siddha</s> women who walk [upon them] —

children.text: sevyo 'yaṃ malayācalaḥ kimapi me cetaḥ karotyutsukam // Nā_1.9 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Malaya</s> mountain, fit for enjoyment, somehow fills my heart with longing. // Nā 1.9 //

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ spandate cakṣuḥ phalākāṅkṣā na me kvacit /
children.translated_text: My right eye throbs; I have no expectation of any fruit anywhere;

children.text: na ca mithyā munivacaḥ kathayiṣyati kiṃ nvidam // Nā_1.10 //
children.translated_text: and the word of a sage is never false — what will this foretell? // Nā 1.10 //
The bark of trees has been stripped out of compassion alone, not too thick, just for the purpose of clothing;
the aged, broken water-pot — [of water] as pure as the sky — is from a mountain stream.
Here and there are seen the girdles of <s>muñja</s> grass broken and discarded by young students,

children.text: nityākarṇanayā śukena ca padaṃ sāmnāmidaṃ paṭhayate // Nā_1.11 //
children.translated_text: and by constant listening, even a parrot here recites a passage of the <s>Sāmans</s> (Sāma Veda hymns). // Nā 1.11 //
With the sound of bees, they seem to sweetly say 'Welcome!';
with their heads bowed low with fruit, they seem to make obeisance.
Showering blossoms upon me, as if offering <s>arghya</s> (water of honor) —
how have even these trees been taught the reception of a guest? // Nā 1.12 //
With the clearly displayed ascending scale showing the registers of low, middle, and high,
as if blending with the string-sound of a humming <s>vīṇā</s> —
these deer, checking the sound of chewing their mouthfuls of grass held between their teeth,
yawn and listen to a song with distinct and graceful notes. // Nā 1.13 //
May my desire be fulfilled, O Blessed One, by your grace! // Nā 1.14 //

body.translated_text: O <s>Gaurī</s>, resplendent with the golden pollen of blossoming lotus stamens! O my [goddess]!

children.translated_text: Here, the expression has been achieved through [all] ten types of expressive syllabic patterns;
the tempo, threefold — quick, medium, and slow — is clearly displayed;
the three kinds of cadences beginning with <s>gopuccha</s> have been accomplished in order;

children.text: stattvaughānugatāśca vādyavidhayaḥ samyak trayo darśitāḥ // Nā_1.15 //
children.translated_text: and the three modes of instrumental music, following the succession of beats, have been properly demonstrated. // Nā 1.15 //
If she is a celestial woman, then the thousand eyes of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>) have attained their purpose;

children.text: rnāgī cenna rasātalaṃ śaśabhṛtā śūnyaṃ mukhe 'syāḥ sthite /
children.translated_text: if she is a <s>Nāgī</s> (serpent maiden), then the nether world is empty with her face's moon standing here above.
If she is of our race, our birth conquers all other races; if she is a <s>Vidyādharī</s>,

children.text: syātsiddhānvayajā yadi tribhuvane siddhā prasiddhāstataḥ // Nā_1.16 //
children.translated_text: she must be of a <s>Siddha</s> lineage — in that case, the <s>Siddhas</s> are celebrated in the three worlds! // Nā 1.16 //

children.text: śramamalaṃ tapasaiva gatā punaḥ kimiti sambhramakāriṇi ! khidyate // Nā_1.17 //
children.translated_text: This body has already endured enough weariness through austerity — why then do you cause such agitation? // Nā 1.17 //

body.translated_text: O you with trembling, wide, long eyes! O you with full, round breasts heaving with sighs!

children.translated_text: This <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance) shines clearly on his head; this <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft) is between his brows;
his eyes rival the lotus; his chest competes with [that of] <s>Hariṇa</s> (a deer / Viṣṇu);

children.text: cakrāṅkañca yathā padadvayamidaṃ manye tathā ko 'pyayaṃ
children.translated_text: and these two feet are marked with wheels — I think that this [person],
whoever he is, will not rest until he has attained the rank of a <s>Vidyādhara</s> emperor. // Nā 1.18 //
[Prakrit:] On one side, the words of my elders; on the other, the joys of seeing the beloved;

children.text: gamaṇāgamaṇādhirūḍhaṃ ajja bi dolaedi me hiaaṃ // Nā_1.19 //
children.translated_text: poised between going and coming, even today my heart swings [like a pendulum]. // Nā 1.19 //
[Sanskrit:] On one side, the words of my elders; on the other, the joys of seeing the beloved;
poised between going and coming, even today my heart swings. // Nā 1.19 //
By this woman, with her broad-hipped gait that obstructs [my path],

children.text: anyato 'pi vrajantyā me hṛdaye nihitaṃ padam // Nā_1.20 //
children.translated_text: even as she goes elsewhere, a step has been placed in my heart. // Nā 1.20 //
Bearing on his temples a pallor from the sandalwood paste ground in that very instant by the heat [of passion],
his face being fanned by the breezes from the flapping of his own ears,
now, this lord of elephants, with his heart specially sprinkled by the spray cast off from his trunk,

children.text: rgāḍhāyallakaduḥsahāmiva daśāṃ dhatte gajānāṃ patiḥ // Nā_1.21 //
children.translated_text: assumes a condition as if the tightly-clinging state [of rut] were unbearable. // Nā 1.21 //
[Prakrit:] Even this [breeze], cooled by contact with the leaves and sprouts of dense sandalwood vines,

children.text: ṇīsāsehiṃ tumaṃ evva kaalīdalamāruaṃ uṇhaṃ // Nā_2.1 //
children.translated_text: you yourself make hot by your sighs, like a dark-petaled wind. // Nā 2.1 //
Turning back with the beauty of her white-and-dark glances upon those trees in the hermitage,
making them appear as if they had bundles of dark deer-skins hanging from their branches —

children.text: yad dṛṣṭosmi tayā munerapi purastenaiva mayyāhate
children.translated_text: since I was seen by her even before the sage, and by that very [glance] I was struck,

children.text: puṣpeṣo ! bhavatā mudhaiva kimiti kṣipyanta ete śarāḥ? // Nā_2.2 //
children.translated_text: O god of flowers! Why do you vainly hurl these arrows? // Nā 2.2 //

body.text: nītāḥ kiṃ na niśāḥ śaśāṅkadhavalā nāghrātamindīvaraṃ?

children.translated_text: Have I not endured the evening breezes fragrant with blossoming <s>mālatī</s>?

children.text: jhaṅkāraḥ kamalākare madhulihāṃ kiṃ vā mayā na śruto?
children.translated_text: Have I not heard the humming of bees in the lotus pond?

children.text: nirvyājaṃ vidhureṣvadhīra iti māṃ yenābhidhatte bhavān? // Nā_2.3 //
children.translated_text: Why then do you truly call me 'faint-hearted among the love-stricken'? // Nā 2.3 //

body.translated_text: Have I not passed nights radiant with moonlight? Have I not smelled the blue lotus?

children.translated_text: The arrows of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One), though they were flower-tipped, were not endured by a woman's heart;

children.text: yenādyaiva purastava vadāmi dhīra iti sa kathamaham? // Nā_2.4 //
children.translated_text: by which [I say] 'steadfast' before you just today — how [can] I [be called that]? // Nā 2.4 //
This bower of sandalwood vines, even with its moonstone slabs, is not dear to me

children.text: candrānanayā rahitaṃ candrikayā mukhamiva niśāyāḥ // Nā_2.5 //
children.translated_text: when devoid of the moon-faced one — like the face of the night without moonlight. // Nā 2.5 //
On this moonstone slab, with her face turned pale,
resting her cheek upon her left lotus-hand, heaving with deep sighs,
with her intention plainly revealed by the slight quivering of her brows,
her mind's displeasure suspended — I saw my beloved weeping. // Nā 2.6 //
As if flowing from this moonrise of your face,
this surface of moonstone slab has been sprinkled by this water of tears. // Nā 2.7 //
Of [this face] whose lips have the beauty of an unstrained <s>bimba</s> fruit, which is a festival for the eyes, like the moon —
even the [mere] outline of [my] beloved's face, seen for the first time, brings happiness. // Nā 2.8 //
My beloved is near — she has been placed before me in imagination;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā likhāmyenāṃ yadi tat ko 'tra vismayaḥ ! // Nā_2.9 //
children.translated_text: having seen [her] again and again, I draw her — if so, what wonder is there in this? // Nā 2.9 //
Since he is the ornament of the <s>Vidyādhara</s> royal lineage, wise, honorable among the good,
unmatched in beauty, rich in valor, learned, modest, and young;
and since, out of compassion for beings, he would even renounce his own life, striving for the welfare of creatures —

children.text: stenāsmai dadataḥ svasāramatulāṃ tuṣṭirviṣādaśca me // Nā_2.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in giving him my incomparable sister, I feel both satisfaction and sorrow. // Nā 2.10 //

children.text: na khalu na khalu mugdhe ! sāhasaṃ kāryamīdṛk
children.translated_text: No, no, O innocent one! Such rashness should not be committed!
Remove this hand, [soft] as a shoot, from the vine!

children.text: kusumamapi vicetuṃ yo na manye samarthaḥ
children.translated_text: He who I do not think capable of plucking even a flower —

children.text: kalayati sa kathaṃ te pāśamudbandhanāya? // Nā_2.11 //
children.translated_text: how would he fashion a noose for your hanging? // Nā 2.11 //
On your neck, fit for a garland of pearls, you have placed a noose;

children.text: gṛhītaḥ sāparādho 'yaṃ kathaṃ te mucyate karaḥ? // Nā_2.12 //
children.translated_text: this hand of yours, having been caught [in the act], is guilty — how can it be released? // Nā 2.12 //

children.text: vṛṣṭayā piṣṭātakasya dyutimiha malaye meyutulyāṃ dadhānaḥ
children.translated_text: On <s>Malaya</s>, assuming a luster equal to the splendor of crushed <s>piṣṭātaka</s> (yellow pigment) from the [seasonal] rains,
whose beauty of twilight glow at the commencement of day is at once surpassed by vermillion,
with the delightful sounds of tinkling anklets on the moving feet of women singing aloud,

children.text: rūdvāhasnānavelāṃ kathayati bhavataḥ siddhaye siddhalokaḥ // Nā_2.13 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Siddhaloka</s> (realm of perfected beings) announces the time for your nuptial bath, for your fulfillment. // Nā_2.13 //
The meeting that arises from mutual sight, of those equal in beauty, love, family, and age,

children.text: keṣāñcideva manye samāgamo bhavati puṇyavatām // Nā_2.14 //
children.translated_text: happens, I think, only for certain fortunate souls. // Nā_2.14 //

children.text: ṇiccaṃ jo pibai suraṃ jaṇassa piasagamaṃ ca jo kuṇai /
children.translated_text: He who always drinks wine and he who brings about the union of people with their beloved —

children.text: maha de do abi devā baladeo kāmadeo a // Nā_3.1 //
children.translated_text: to me, these two are indeed gods: <s>Baladeva</s> and <s>Kāmadeva</s>. // Nā_3.1 //
On whose chest resides compassion, on whose face dwells intoxication scented with blue lotuses,

children.text: sīsammi a seharao ṇiccaṃ via saṃṭhiā jassa // Nā_3.2 //
children.translated_text: and on whose head the crest-jewel is forever established — // Nā_3.2 //

children.text: hariharapidāmahāṇaṃ pi gavvido jo ṇa jāṇai ṇamiduṃ /
children.translated_text: He who, proud even before <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Pitāmaha</s>, knows not how to bow —

children.text: so seharao calaṇesu tujja ṇomālie padai // Nā_3.3 //
children.translated_text: that crest-jewel falls at your feet, O <s>Nōmālie</s>! // Nā_3.3 //
When seen, she casts her gaze downward; when addressed, she makes no reply;
on the bed she turns away and remains still; when embraced by force, she trembles.
When her friends depart from the bedchamber, she herself strives to leave —

children.text: jātā vāmatayaiva me 'dya sutarāṃ prityai navoḍhā priyā // Nā_3.4 //
children.translated_text: my newly-wed beloved has today become all the more delightful through her very coyness. // Nā_3.4 //
That silence which was maintained as a reply to me when I uttered a reproachful 'hum!',
that this body was heated by moonbeams as if by the blazing flames of a forest fire,
that many nights and days were spent in meditation by a mind not bowing to another, O beloved!

children.text: tasyaitat tapasaḥ phalaṃ mukhamidaṃ paśyāmi yatte 'dhunā // Nā_3.5 //
children.translated_text: The fruit of all that <s>tapas</s> (penance) is this — that I now behold your face. // Nā_3.5 //

body.text: khedāya stanabhāra eva kimu te madhyasya hāro 'paraḥ?

children.translated_text: Your thighs are exhausted by the weight of your hips — what further purpose does this girdle serve?

children.text: śaktiḥ pādayugatya norupugalaṃ voḍhu kuto nūpurau?
children.translated_text: Your feet scarcely have the strength to bear your own limbs — whence then anklets too?

children.text: svāṅgaireva vimūṣitāsi vahasi kleśāya kiṃ maṇḍanam? // Nā_3.6 //
children.translated_text: You are adorned by your own body alone — why do you wear ornaments only to suffer? // Nā_3.6 //

body.translated_text: Is not the burden of your breasts itself enough to weary your waist — what need of a necklace besides?

children.translated_text: The flow of sandal-paste cools the floor of the vine-bower to its very edges;

children.text: nārād dhārāgṛhāṇāṃ dhvanimanu tatute tāṇḍavaṃ nolakaṇṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: nearby, the peacock dances in rhythm to the sound of the fountain-houses.
Released with force from the water-machine, this flood of water fills the basins around the trees,
made tawny-yellow by the flower pollen shaken loose by the force of its fall. // Nā_3.7 //
These bees, whose vine-bower grounds are made resonant by the beginnings of song,
mingled with the pollen of flowers and the fragrance of fine garments,
drinking deeply of the honey-nectar together with their companion-bees,
seem to be celebrating a drinking festival on all sides. // Nā_3.8 //
Their limbs anointed with yellow sandalwood, wearing garlands of <s>Santānaka</s> (wish-fulfilling) flowers,
their white garments made variegated by the play of light from ruby ornaments,
these <s>Vidyādharas</s> (celestial sorcerers), together with the <s>Siddha</s> folk, drink the remaining wine
left over by their beloveds, mingling together in the shade of sandalwood trees. // Nā_3.9 //

children.text: etanmukhaṃ priyāyāḥ śaśinaṃ jitvā kapolayāḥ kāntyā /
children.translated_text: This face of my beloved, having conquered the moon by the radiance of her cheeks,
now, warmed by passion, surely strives to conquer the lotus as well. // Nā_3.10 //
This face of yours, graced by the creeper of your brows, with lips like reddish petals —
this is the <s>Nandana</s> garden; everything else is merely a forest. // Nā_3.11 //
On the petals of your lips, one sees the blossoming of your smile-flowers;

children.text: phalaṃ tvanyatra mugdhākṣi ! cakṣuṣormama paśyataḥ // Nā_3.12 //
children.translated_text: but the fruit, O innocent-eyed one, is elsewhere — in my eyes that behold you. // Nā_3.12 //
Touched by the rays of the sun, bearing a rosy hue,
its filaments made visible by the creeping rays of your teeth —

children.text: ayi makhamidaṃ mugdhe ! satyaṃ samaṃ kamalena te
children.translated_text: O innocent one, truly this face of yours rivals the lotus,

children.text: madhu madhukaraḥ kintvetasmin pibbanna vibhāvyate? // Nā_3.13 //
children.translated_text: yet why is no bee seen drinking honey from it? // Nā_3.13 //
Without slaying that rival, how can I, shameless as I am,

children.text: kathayiṣyāmi hṛtaṃ tava rājyaṃ rīpuṇeti nirlajjaḥ? // Nā_3.14 //
children.translated_text: tell <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s> that his kingdom has been seized by an enemy? // Nā_3.14 //
With aerial chariots that creep in every direction, traversing all the pathways of the sky,
darkening the daylight like the rainy season by concealing the rays of the sun,

children.text: ete yātāśca sadyastava vacanamitaḥ prāpya yuddhāya siddhāḥ
children.translated_text: these <s>Siddhas</s>, having received your command, have swiftly gone forth to battle,
and your sovereignty, sealed with the mark of the destruction and submission of rebellious enemies, is accomplished. // Nā_3.15 //
Even by me alone, blazing with the mass of radiant sword-rays drawn forth in fury,

children.text: ārānnipatya hariṇeva mataṅgajendramājau mataṅgahatakaṃ viddhi // Nā_3.16 //
children.translated_text: rushing upon him from afar like a lion upon a lordly elephant — know that the wretch <s>Mataṅga</s> has been slain in battle! // Nā_3.16 //

children.text: svaśarīramapi parārthe yaḥ khalu dadyādayācitaḥ kṛpayā /
children.translated_text: He who would give even his own body for another's sake, unasked, out of compassion —

children.text: rājyasya kṛte sa kathaṃ prāṇivadhakrauryamanumanute // Nā_3.17 //
children.translated_text: how would he consent to the cruelty of slaying living beings for the sake of a kingdom? // Nā_3.17 //
Dispelling the bee from the lotus-bud where it had sealed itself in the clasp of sleep,
gladdening the entire world with his rays, devoted solely to the task of fulfilling all hopes,
beheld by <s>Siddhas</s> whose mouths are busy with continuous praise, even as he sets,

children.text: ekaḥ ślāghyo vivasvān parahitakaraṇāyaiva yasya prayāsaḥḥ // Nā_3.18 //
children.translated_text: the Sun alone is praiseworthy — he whose every effort is only for the benefit of others. // Nā_3.18 //

children.text: antaḥpurāṇāṃ vihitavyavasthaḥ pade pade 'haṃ skhalanāni rakṣan /
children.translated_text: Having arranged the affairs of the inner apartments, guarding against stumbles at every step,

children.text: jarāturaḥ samprati daṇḍanītyā sarvāṃ nṛpasyānukaromi vṛttim // Nā_4.1 //
children.translated_text: aged and infirm, I now carry out the king's entire conduct through the rod of governance. // Nā_4.1 //
The bed is a grassy meadow, the seat a clean stone, the dwelling beneath the trees;

children.text: śītaṃ nirjharavāri pānamaśanaṃ kandāḥ sahāyā mṛgāḥ /
children.translated_text: the drink is cool waterfall-water, the food is roots, the companions are deer.
In the forest where all such provisions are obtained without asking, there is but this one fault:
that one lives in vain among those whose efforts to serve others are fruitless, since those in need are hard to find. // Nā_4.2 //
Surging upward from the forceful striking of the lord of aquatic elephants emerging from the water,
making all the mountain caves and cavern-spaces resound with echoes,
this sound rises loudly, churning the pathway of the ears, and just as it does,
this shore-tide, white as innumerable conch shells swaying, seems to approach. // Nā_4.3 //
With water made fragrant by the scent of clove-blossoms chewed by the trunk-tip of the elephant of the sea,
this ocean-shore shines, tinted with the luster of gems. // Nā_4.4 //

children.text: jihvāsahasradvitayasya madhye naikāpi sā tasya kimasti jihvā /
children.translated_text: Among the two thousand tongues of that one, is there not even a single tongue

children.text: ekāhirakṣārthamahidviṣe 'dya datto mayātmeti yayā bravīti // Nā_4.5 //
children.translated_text: by which he could say, 'For the protection of one serpent, I have today given myself to the enemy of serpents'? // Nā_4.5 //

children.text: ityeṣa bhogipatinā vihitavyavastho yān bhakṣayatyahipatīn patagādhirājaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, by the arrangement made by the lord of serpents, the serpent-kings whom the sovereign of birds devours —

children.text: yāsyanti yānti ca gatāśca dinairbivṛddhiṃ teṣāmamī tuhinaśailaruco 'sthikūṭāḥ // Nā_4.6 //
children.translated_text: those who have gone, those who go now, and those who will go — their numbers only grow day by day; these bone-heaps have the whiteness of the snowy mountain. // Nā_4.6 //
For the sake of this body, which is a receptacle of all impurity, ungrateful and perishable,

children.text: śarīrakasyāpi kṛte mūḍhāḥ pāpāni kurvate ! // Nā_4.7 //
children.translated_text: the deluded commit sins! // Nā_4.7 //
When impermanence first embraces the newborn,

children.text: dhātrīva jananī paścāttadā śokasya kaḥ kramaḥ? // Nā_4.8 //
children.translated_text: like a nurse before the mother — then what scope is there for grief? // Nā_4.8 //

body.text:
mūḍhāyā muhuraśrusantatimucaḥ kṛtvā pralāpān bahūn
kastrātā tava putraketi kṛpaṇaṃ dikṣu kṣipantyā dṛśam /
aṅke māturavasthitaṃ śiśumimaṃ tyaktvā ghṛṇāmaśnataḥ
cañcurnaiva khagādhipasya hṛdayaṃ vajreṇa manye kṛtam/9 //
body.translated_text: Of the foolish mother who repeatedly sheds streams of tears, making many lamentations, pitifully casting her gaze in all directions crying 'Who will save your child?' — abandoning this infant resting in his mother's lap and devouring him without mercy, the beak of the lord of birds — I think his heart is not made of diamond. // Nā_4.9 //

children.translated_text: Those supremely compassionate ones who never refused the prayers of supplicants,

children.text: yaiḥ kāruṇyaparigrahānna gaṇitaḥ svārthaḥ parārtha prati /
children.translated_text: who, out of the embrace of compassion, did not reckon their own interests against the interests of others,
those noble beings whose minds were pained by the suffering of others — they have all passed away.

children.text: mātaḥ ! saṃhara bāṣpavegamadhunā kasyāgrato rudyate? // Nā_4.10 //
children.translated_text: O Mother! Restrain this torrent of tears — before whom now does one weep? // Nā_4.10 //
One who is afflicted, whose life has reached the throat, abandoned by his own kinsmen —

children.text: trāye nainaṃ yadi tataḥ kaḥ śarīreṇa me guṇaḥ // Nā_4.11 //
children.translated_text: if I do not save him, then what use is this body of mine? // Nā_4.11 //
Seeing her distress, I think this bewilderment arises from a mother's love for her child;
even the enemy of serpents, hard-hearted though he be, would feel compassion. // Nā_4.12 //
He whose fierce beak is smeared with streams of blood from splitting open the skulls of great serpents —

children.text: kvāsau garutmān kva ca nāma saumyasvabhāvarūpākṛtireṣa sādhuḥ? // Nā_4.13 //
children.translated_text: where is that <s>Garutmān</s> (divine eagle), and where indeed is this gentle being, mild in nature and form, this saint? // Nā_4.13 //
Place upon my shoulder this mark of the victim, and covering myself, I shall go before the son of <s>Vinatā</s>;

children.text: putrasya te jīvitarakṣaṇāya svadehamāhārayituṃ dadāmi // Nā_4.14 //
children.translated_text: to save the life of your son, I offer my own body as food. // Nā_4.14 //
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> once ate dog-flesh like an outcaste — for what purpose;
<s>Nādijaṅgha</s> was slain, having received a favor from him — for what purpose, by <s>Gautama</s>;
this son of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), devours serpents daily — for what purpose;

children.text: prāṇāṃstāneṣa sādhustṛṇamiva kṛpayā yaḥ parārtha dadāti // Nā_4.15 //
children.translated_text: it is for that purpose that this noble one gives away his life like grass, out of compassion, for the sake of others. // Nā_4.15 //

children.text: jāyante ca mriyante ca mādṛśāḥ kṣudrajantavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Insignificant creatures like me are born and die constantly;
but the birth of those like you, who have girded themselves for the service of others — how rare is that? // Nā_4.16 //

children.text: mriyate mriyamāṇe yā tvayi jīvati jīvati /
children.translated_text: She who dies when you die and lives when you live —

children.text: tāṃ yadīcchasi jīvantīṃ rakṣātmānaṃ mamāsubhiḥ // Nā_4.17 //
children.translated_text: if you wish her to live, then protect yourself with my life-breaths. // Nā_4.17 //
With greed swelling from the morsels of half-torn, dripping flesh plucked up by his darting beak,
with thick darkness formed by the pair of outspread wings fanning away the twilight of [those consumed in] splendor,
the rows of flame-crests of <s>Śiva's</s> [fires], blown from their mouths, fall silently
in this [place], resounding with the ever-flowing, thick, oily streams [of fat from] the cremation ground. // Nā 4.18 //
With the daily, unceasing feeding of serpents [to <s>Garuḍa</s>], with the satisfaction bestowed by <s>Vināyaka</s>,
this cremation ground, with its moon-white skull-cups, appears like the terrifying body [of <s>Rudra</s>]. // Nā 4.19 //
We beseech you, O Mother, in whatever birth we may go,

children.text: tasyāṃ tasyāṃ priyasute ! mātā bhūyāstvameva naḥ // Nā_4.20 //
children.translated_text: in each one, O dear son, may you alone be our mother! // Nā 4.20 //
This pair of red garments has arrived at the appointed time;
it brings great joy to one who sacrifices his body for the sake of others. // Nā 4.21 //

children.text: tulyāḥ saṃvarttakābhraīḥ pidadhati gaganaṃ paṅktayaḥ pakṣatīnāṃ
children.translated_text: Rows of wings, equal to the clouds of universal dissolution, cover the sky;

children.text: tīre vegānilo 'mbhaḥ kṣipati bhuva iva lāvanāyāmburāśeḥ /
children.translated_text: the wind of his speed hurls the waters of the salt ocean upon the shore as if upon the earth;

children.text: kurvan kalpāntaśaṅkāṃ sapadi ca sabhayaṃ vīkṣito digdvipendrai-
children.translated_text: causing the fear of the end of an age, and immediately gazed upon with terror by the lord-elephants of the directions,
the radiance of his body, with the brilliance of twelve suns, repeatedly tints the ten directions tawny. // Nā 4.22 //

children.text: na tathā sukhayati manye malayavatī malayacandanarasārdrā /
children.translated_text: Not so much does the embrace of <s>Malayavatī</s>, moist with the essence of <s>Malaya</s> sandalwood, delight me, I think,
as this sacrificial stone, embraced for the fulfillment of one's cherished purpose. // Nā 4.23 //

children.text: śayitena māturaṅke visrabdhaṃ śaiśave na tat prāptam /
children.translated_text: That happiness was not obtained by sleeping trustfully on my mother's lap in childhood,

children.text: labdhaṃ sukhaṃ mayāsyā vadhyaśilāyā yadutsaṅge // Nā_4.24 //
children.translated_text: which I have gained in the lap of this sacrificial stone. // Nā 4.24 //
Having cast away the disc of the moon, rubbing the remaining body in a circle made by fear,
he was joyfully seen by his elder brother when <s>Pūṣan</s> (the Sun) was shaken by the rushing of his chariot-horses;
this one, his wings become elongated with trailing masses of clouds at their edges,
has reached the coastal mountain <s>Malaya</s> in an instant, greedy for the feast of the great serpent. // Nā 4.25 //
By protecting the serpent today, the merit I have earned through the gift of my own body —

children.text: bhave bhave tena mamaivamevaṃ bhūyāt parārthaḥ khalu dehalābhaḥ // Nā_4.26 //
children.translated_text: by that, in birth after birth, may the obtaining of a body be thus for the sake of others! // Nā 4.26 //
To save the remaining serpents, I lie fallen on this sacrificial stone;
now with his beak, more terrible than a thunderbolt-staff, piercing my chest,
I swiftly lift up the serpent for him to eat, wrapped in a red garment,
smeared, as it were, with blood flowing from [the serpent's] heart, torn open by fear of me. // Nā 4.27 //

children.text: svarge kiṃ vaiṣa cakraṃ mukharayati diśāṃ dundubhīnāṃ ninādaḥ?
children.translated_text: Is this the sound of celestial drums resounding in the directions, with a wheel [of glory] in heaven?

children.text: āṃ jñātaṃ ! so 'pi manye mama javamarutā kampitaḥ pārijātaḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, I understand! I think that <s>Pārijāta</s> tree has been shaken by the swift wind of mine;
and this rumbling too is by all the clouds of dissolution, seized with fear of the end. // Nā 4.28 //

body.translated_text: Is this a shower of flowers falling from the sky, with bees delighted by the fragrance?

children.text: nāgānāṃ rakṣitā bhāti gurureṣa yathā mama /
children.translated_text: This teacher of mine shines as the protector of the <s>Nāgas</s>;
clearly, he will today remove the desire of the serpent-eater (<s>Garuḍa</s>) [to consume them]. // Nā 4.29 //
Even when a loved one is in one's own garden at home, evil is feared out of love;
how much more when he stands in the midst of a frightful wilderness with many dangers! // Nā 5.1 //
Wearing linen with folds, undulating at the edges, resembling foam and water,
resplendent with the queen of great merit at his side, like [the Gaṅgā with its banks],
<s>Jīmūtaketu</s> bears a beauty well-suited to the ocean,
with <s>Malayavatī</s> at his side appearing like the seashore. // Nā 5.2 //
The pleasures of youth have been enjoyed, fame has been scattered abroad,
the kingdom has been held with firm resolve, and austerity too has been practiced;
the son is praiseworthy, this daughter-in-law is of fitting lineage —

children.text: cintyo māya nanu kṛtārthatayādya mṛtyuḥ // Nā_5.3 //
children.translated_text: surely death should be contemplated by me now with the thought 'I am fulfilled.' // Nā 5.3 //
Why do you throb, O left [eye]! — repeatedly indicating misfortune to me?

children.text: hatacakṣurapahataṃ te sphuritaṃ mama putrakaḥ kuśalī // Nā_5.4 //
children.translated_text: Accursed eye! May your throbbing be nullified — may my little son be well! // Nā 5.4 //
As it is being watched, causing extreme anguish to the eyes, releasing its own rays of reddish light —

children.text: utpātavātatalīkṛtatārakābhametatpuraḥ patati kiṃ sahasā nabhastaḥ? // Nā_5.5 //
children.translated_text: what is this that falls suddenly from the sky before us, like a star shaken by a whirlwind? // Nā 5.5 //
Of the serpents being devoured by <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) in great numbers,
their crest-jewels fall like this, in the form of meteors. // Nā 5.6 //

children.text: gokarṇamarṇavataṭe tvaritaṃ praṇamya prāpto 'smi tāṃ khalu bhujaṅgamavadhyabhūmim /
children.translated_text: Having hastily bowed at <s>Gokarṇa</s> on the ocean shore, I have reached that very sacrificial ground of serpents;

children.text: āḍhāya taṃ nakhamukhakṣatasañca vidyādharaṃ gaganamutpatito garutmān ! // Nā_5.7 //
children.translated_text: having seized that <s>Vidyādhara</s> wounded by his talons, <s>Garutmān</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) has flown up into the sky! // Nā 5.7 //
I have not gained the single glory of protecting the serpents, nor has the praiseworthy command of my lord been carried out;

children.text: dattvātmānaṃ rakṣito 'nyena śocyo hā dhik ! kaṣṭaṃ ! vañcito vañcito 'smi // Nā_5.8 //
children.translated_text: having given up his own life, he was saved by another — alas, shame! How wretched! I am deceived, deceived! // Nā 5.8 //
At first, fallen sparsely on the ground, in large drops, then
scattered in fine particles from the impact on the rocks, swarming with insects on the flat areas,
difficult to discern on the mineral-stained rock-face, dark-hued in its natural form on the dense peak —

children.text: menāṃ tākṣya didṛkṣurnipuṇamanusaran raktadhārāṃ vrajāmi // Nā_5.9 //
children.translated_text: wishing to see him, I follow this trail of blood carefully as I go, O <s>Tārkṣya</s>! // Nā 5.9 //

children.text: mayi saṅkrāntametatte yena sahyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Nā_5.10 //
children.translated_text: which has passed over to me from you, so that it may become bearable. // Nā 5.10 //

body.translated_text: Convey my own unbearable grief, O son!,

children.translated_text: By some <s>Vidyādhara</s> whose heart was seized with compassion,

children.text: mama saṃrakṣitāḥ prāṇā dattvātmānaṃ garutmatte // Nā_5.11 //
children.translated_text: my life-breaths were saved, while he gave his own body to <s>Garutmat</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>). // Nā 5.11 //
By making the crest-jewel fall at my feet, you,
even though you have gone to the other world, have not abandoned the order of courtesy! // Nā 5.12 //
With the head deeply bowed from devotion, prostrating constantly at my feet,

children.text: cūḍāmaṇirnikaṣaṇaurmasṛṇo 'pyahiṃstraḥ gāḍhaṃ vidārayati me hṛdayaṃ kathaṃ nu? // Nā_5.13 //
children.translated_text: the crest-jewel, though smooth from the polishing [of prostrations], though non-violent — how does it deeply tear my heart? // Nā 5.13 //
Making the mountain slopes like troughs with the scratching of his blood-moist beak,
with his scorching-edged [eyes], the rows of flame from his own eye-light entering the interstices,
with the ground pierced deep by the tips of his fierce, diamond-hard talons,
the enemy of serpents (<s>Garuḍa</s>) is seen from afar on the summit of <s>Malaya</s> mountain. // Nā 5.14 //
Though his blood is being drunk in excess, there is no languor in this ocean of fortitude;
even while bearing the pains of his flesh being torn, his face is serene;

children.text: gātraṃ yanna viluptameṣa pulakastatra sphuṭo lakṣyate
children.translated_text: the part of his body that has not yet been consumed — there a distinct horripilation is visible;
his gaze falls upon me, [his] benefactor, as if without malice even now. // Nā 5.15 //

children.text: śirāmukhaiḥ syandata eva raktamadyāpi dehe mama māṃsabhasti /
children.translated_text: Blood still flows from the mouths of my veins, and flesh yet remains on my body —

children.text: tṛptiṃ na paśyāmi tavāpi tāvat kiṃ bhakṣaṇāttvaṃ virato garutman! // Nā_5.16 //
children.translated_text: I do not see your satisfaction yet; then why have you ceased eating, O <s>Garutman</s>! // Nā 5.16 //

children.text: āvarjitaṃ mayā cañcvā hṛdayāt tava śoṇitam /
children.translated_text: I have drawn blood from your heart with my beak;

children.text: anena dhairyyeṇa punastvayā hṛdayameva naḥ // Nā_5.17 //
children.translated_text: but with this fortitude, you have in turn [drawn] our very heart. // Nā 5.17 //

body.text: āstāṃ svastikalakṣma vakṣasi tanau nālokyate kañcukaḥ

children.text: jihve jalpata eva me na gaṇite nāma tvayā dve api !
children.translated_text: O tongue! Even while you speak, two names are not counted by you!
The three [heads] with gem-luster concealed by the veil of thick poison-fire smoke,
and these hoods, swollen by the wind of sighs born from unbearable grief — do you not see them! // Nā 5.18 //

body.translated_text: Let the <s>svastika</s> mark on my chest be — the armor on my body is not noticed;

children.translated_text: On <s>Meru</s>, in the caves of <s>Mandara</s>, on the slopes of <s>Himavat</s>, on the great <s>Mahendra</s> mountain,
on the rocky surfaces of <s>Kailāsa</s>, in the regions of the eastern slopes of <s>Malaya</s>,

children.text: uddeśeṣvapi teṣu teṣu bahuśo yasya śrutaṃ tanmayā /
children.translated_text: in those various places, I have often heard
the fame [of <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>] being sung by hosts who traverse the boundaries of the worlds. // Nā 5.19 //
Having protected my body from <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) with his own body,

children.text: yuktaṃ netuṃ bhavatā pātālatalādapi talaṃ mām? // Nā_5.20 //
children.translated_text: is it proper for you to bring me even lower than the nether world? // Nā 5.20 //

body.text: ātmīyaḥ para ityayaṃ khalu kutaḥ satyaṃ kṛpāyāḥ kramaḥ?

children.text: kiṃ rakṣāmi bahūn kimekamiti te jātā na cintā katham?
children.translated_text: 'Shall I protect many, or one?' — how did this thought not arise in you?
In saving a serpent from <s>Tārkṣya</s>, by sacrificing your own life,

children.text: yenātmā pitarau vadhūriti hataṃ niḥśeṣametatkulam // Nā_5.21 //
children.translated_text: you have destroyed this entire family — yourself, your parents, and your wife. // Nā 5.21 //

body.translated_text: 'This one is mine, that one is another's' — truly, from where does compassion follow such order?

children.translated_text: With the tips of his tongues of <s>Kāla</s> (Time), flickering with the relish of devouring the three worlds, resembling broken flames,
creeping [tongues] capable of swallowing the seven oceans as if they were drops of ghee,
with his wing-winds, more powerful than the gusts of the final cataclysmic storm, fanned at will —
I shall fall into this submarine fire (<s>Vāḍavāgni</s>), terrifying with the conflagration at the end of the age. // Nā 5.22 //
My son, whose remaining limbs have been consumed, his life-breaths departing to the region of the throat

children.text: prāṇāṃstyajantaṃ tanayaṃ nirīkṣya kathaṃ na pāpaḥ śatadhā vrajāmi // Nā_5.23 //
children.translated_text: as if seeking refuge due to being shelterless — beholding him dying, how do I, the sinful one, not burst into a hundred pieces! // Nā 5.23 //
In this aggregate of fat, bones, flesh, marrow, and blood, covered with skin,

children.text: śarīranāmni kā śobhā sadā bībhatsadarśane? // Nā_5.24 //
children.translated_text: called 'body,' always repulsive to behold — what beauty is there? // Nā 5.24 //
Cease forever from the slaughter of living beings! Feel remorse for what was done before!
With effort, accumulate a stream of merit, granting fearlessness to all beings,

children.text: magnaṃ yenātra nainaḥ phalati pariṇataṃ prāṇihiṃsāsamutthaṃ
children.translated_text: so that the sin arising from violence to living beings, which has matured, may not bear fruit, being submerged [in merit]
into the fathomless flood of waters, like a lump of salt cast into the depths of a lake. (25)
I, who was sleeping in the slumber of ignorance, have been awakened by you;
from this day forth, I am desisted from the killing of all living beings. (26)
Sometimes appearing like islands with their vast coils spread out like sandbanks,
sometimes whirling in eddies with their bodies coiled in circles,

children.text: vrajan kūlāt kūlaṃ kvacidapi ca setupratisamaḥ
children.translated_text: sometimes moving from shore to shore, sometimes resembling bridges themselves --

children.text: samājo nāgānāṃ viharatu mahodanvati sukham // Nā_5.27 //
children.translated_text: may this assembly of <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) sport happily in the great ocean! (27)
Bearing their dark tresses of hair, hanging loose and disheveled, black as dense darkness,
their cheeks coppery from the touch of the first rays of the sun, as though smeared with <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion),
their limbs languid with exertion yet heedless of their wounds, in this forest of sandalwood trees --

children.text: masmin gāyantu rāgāduragayuvatayaḥ kīrtimetāṃ tavaiva // Nā_5.28 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>Nāga</s> maidens sing with passion this very fame of yours! (28)
Imagining you torn open by the beak-tip of <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>),

children.text: tvadūduḥkhaduḥkhitā nūnamāste sā jananī tava // Nā_5.29 //
children.translated_text: grieving at your suffering, surely that mother of yours now sits in anguish. (29)

children.text: gātrāṇyamūni na vahanti sacetanatvaṃ śrātraṃ sphuṭākṣarapadāṃ na diraṃ śrṛṇoti /
children.translated_text: These limbs no longer bear consciousness; the ear no longer hears speech with clear syllables and words;

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ nimītilamidaṃ sahasaiva cakṣurhā tāta ! yānti vivaśasya mamāsavo 'mī // Nā_5.30 //
children.translated_text: alas, this eye has suddenly closed -- O father! These life-breaths of mine, helpless, are departing! (30)

children.text: nirādhāraṃ dhairyya kamiva śaraṇaṃ yātu vinayaḥ?
children.translated_text: Where shall firmness, now without support, find refuge? Where shall humility go?

children.text: kṣamaḥ kṣāntiṃ voḍhuṃ ka iha viratā dānaparatā /
children.translated_text: Who here is capable of bearing patience? Devotion to giving has ceased;

children.text: hataṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ vrajatu kṛpaṇā kvādya karuṇā?
children.translated_text: truth is slain -- truly! Where shall wretched compassion go now?

children.text: jagajjātaṃ śūnyaṃ tvayi tanaya lokāntaragate // Nā_5.31 //
children.translated_text: The world has become empty, O son, now that you have departed to the other world. (31)
The lord of waters uplifted by my wings, driven by swiftest-rushing winds,
the twelve suns falling in a blazing swoon from the fire of my eyes, ablaze,
crushing with my beak the thunderbolt of <s>Śakra</s>, the mace of <s>Dhana</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), the club of <s>Gada</s>, and the staff of the Lord of the Dead (<s>Yama</s>) --

children.text: ājau nirjatya devān kṣaṇamamṛtamayīṃ vṛsṭimabhyutsṛjāmi // Nā_5.32 //
children.translated_text: conquering the gods in battle, I shall in an instant release a shower of nectar! (32)
This <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) gleams manifest upon his head; this is the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft) between his brows;
his eyes rival the lotus; his chest competes with <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>);

children.text: cakrāṅkau caraṇau tathāpi hi kathaṃ hā vatsa madūduṣkṛtai-
children.translated_text: his feet bear the <s>cakra</s> (wheel) marks -- and yet, alas, O child, due to my own misdeeds,
you rest here without attaining the station of <s>Vidyādhara</s>-<s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign of the knowledge-bearers)! (33)
Even with your own life, you who are a benefactor to all beings --

children.text: parituṣṭāsmi te vatsa ! jīva jīmūtavāhana // Nā_5.34 //
children.translated_text: I am fully pleased with you, O child! Live, <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>! (34)

children.text: caraṇau namāmyahaṃ te vidyāvarapūjite ! gauri ! // Nā_5.35 //
children.translated_text: I bow at your feet, O <s>Gaurī</s>, honored by the choicest of <s>vidyās</s> (sacred knowledge)! (35)

body.translated_text: O you who grant boons exceeding all desires! O you who remove the afflictions of those who bow before you! O refuge!

children.translated_text: Having regained their unbroken bodies, radiant with the gleaming gems on their outspread hoods,
licking the ground with the tips of their forked tongues in eager relish of the taste of nectar,
now surging forward with unrestrained speed, like the flood-waters of the rivers of <s>Malaya</s> mountain,
the serpent lords enter the ocean by winding departure-paths! (36)
With the supremely purifying waters that have arisen from my mind-lake (<s>Mānasa</s>), frequented by swans,
freed from mud through contact with lotus pollen,
having come forth and been placed in jeweled vessels fashioned at will -- with these I myself

children.text: tvāṃ vidyādharacakravarttinamahaṃ prītyā karomi kṣaṇāt // Nā_5.37 //
children.translated_text: shall now with joy anoint you as <s>Vidyādhara</s>-<s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign of the knowledge-bearers) in an instant! (37)
Let this golden she-tortoise go before you; here is a white elephant with four tusks;

children.text: śyāmo harirmalayavatyapi cetyamūni ratnāni te samavalokya cakravarttin ! // Nā_5.38 //
children.translated_text: a dark-hued <s>Hari</s> (horse), and also <s>Malayavatī</s> (a queen) -- behold these treasures, O <s>Cakravartin</s>! (38)
This <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> has been saved from the jaws of the lord of birds; the son of <s>Vinatā</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) has been subdued;

children.text: stena prāgbhakṣitā ye viṣadharapatayo jīvitāste 'pi sarve /
children.translated_text: those serpent lords who were formerly devoured by him have all been restored to life;
my life-breaths, not relinquished by my elders, are freed; sovereignty as <s>cakravartin</s> has been attained;

children.text: sākṣāttvaṃ devi ! dṛṣṭā priyamaparamataḥ kiṃ punaḥ prārthyate yat // Nā_5.39 //
children.translated_text: you, O <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), have been seen face to face -- what greater joy remains to be desired? (39)
May the clouds release their rains, their crests dancing with joyful peacocks, at the proper season;
may they make the earth a cloak of continuously thriving golden crops of <s>Hari</s> (grain);
may people, free from calamities and gathering merits, with generous hearts free from envy,

children.text: rmodantāṃ satataṃ ca bāndhavasuhṛdgoṣṭhipramodāḥ prajāḥ // Nā_5.40 //
children.translated_text: ever rejoice in the delights of gatherings with kinsmen and friends! (40)
May there be well-being for all the world; may all beings be devoted to the welfare of others;

children.text: doṣāḥ prayāntu nāśaṃ sarvatra sukhī bhavatu lokaḥ // Nā_5.41 //
children.translated_text: may all faults be destroyed; may the world everywhere be happy! (41)
